open_questions: 1 INCLUDED, SCOPE OPEN (FLAG_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW): the earlier preparation jobs in this design folder (analogy_repair_t4_job attempt 1 $0.5596 and attempt 2 $0.67, aws_probe_job $0.4834, hset1a_aws_job attempt 1 $0.0223 and attempt 2 $0.1827; total $1.9180, watcher figures, not program-validated) are counted conservatively as the prior-spend row PRIOR ($1.92), per Codex 'Envelope consequences' (c3a128ee). Whether they belong inside the $60.00 stays the owner's scope decision. The $0.10 allowance per job (+$0.50) is not added; the state file shows that total.

2 DECIDED (Codex Q2): the $60.00 caps study charges, bounded across all attempts and required remaining work (this program's worst-case spend). The $15.00 launcher bookings are bookkeeping reservations, not invoices; they are never refunded or rewritten; C's $90 and B's $120 booking figures do not raise the ceiling; the canonical campaign cap must also pass on its own (outside this program).
3 DECIDED (Codex Q3/Q6): the third main attempt is normally M3 after M1 and M2; the stop counts every main attempt that started an instance (see owner_stop.counting).

4 DECIDED (Codex Q1): the S1 capacity-refusal accounting rule is ACCEPTED, conditional on the pinned provider failure evidence (provider_0025.json, sha256 d866fbf5...), zero retries, no instance or volume left and the temporary resources removed; the program names that evidence with every report. S1's canonical $15 booking stays. Never reused for an ambiguous launched job.

5 OPEN (FLAG_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW): the $0.10 allowance covers 12 months of retention; the plan's horizon was execution + 30 days after E1; the evidence buckets have no end date. Codex: keep both assumptions visible; reconcile object sizes, transfer, requests and retention before the final freeze; report ongoing charges beyond the bound.

6-9 DECIDED (Codex Q6-Q9): a launched-then-failed main job counts as started; a never-admitted row may be CANCELLED_NOT_LAUNCHED; a wrong source, bundle, worker or checker invalidates the result and blocks the study while cleanup is still inspected; one admission authorizes one RunInstances attempt, and a retry is a new attempt row with its own admission. See REVIEW.md 'v2 (Codex Q1-Q9)'.

10 OPEN (for the runner and the launchers; the gate refuses until they hold): every launcher must write worker_sha256 and checker_sha256 where IDENTITY_FIELDS reads them; the prepare scripts must take the admitted source commit instead of HEAD; the runner runs --launch-check immediately before RunInstances; a training job is prepared after its admission and launched inside the 300-s validity, because its receipt shows no launch time but the job id's preparation time.

rules.admission: row PLANNED (a slot row, or an appended attempt row); nothing RUNNING; the single-writer lock taken; no DONE receipt rejected; no receipt identity shared; no unconfirmed cleanup; no limit breach, wrong identity or uncertain main start; no cancelled mandatory row for a main admission; slots file and program committed and at the fetched remote tip; spent upper bound + this cap + every other reserved mandatory cap (E1 included) <= ceiling; owner stop not triggered; one source per training arm. ADMIT writes the row RUNNING with its admission record, valid 300 s, single use; run --launch-check immediately before the one RunInstances attempt
rules.owner_stop: before every admission while fewer than 3 main training attempts (rows marked counts_toward_training_stop) have started an instance: if the spend upper bound is strictly greater than $30.00, stop: every admission is refused and the runner reports to the owner. Settled rows only move forward, so once triggered the stop stays triggered
rules.rounding: every bound rounded UP to the cent; exact decimals, no floats
